newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks power to sharply higher close.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks power to sharply higher close.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed sharply higher on Wednesday, prompted by the jump by U.S. stocks and bonds on benign U.S. inflation report, brokers said.
"There is a very strong correlation between the U.S. (long) bond market and Hong Kong, so the market is adjusting to the rally in bonds last night," said Gary Wong, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
The Hang Seng Index climbed 239.29 points, or 1.94 percent, to close at 12,581.31, but off its high for the day of 12,613.86.
Trading was brisk, brokers said, and turnover jumped to a hefty HK$10.15 billion, higher Tuesday's HK$9.11 billion.

The benchmark U.S. 30-year Treasury bond gained 30/32 to 94-8/32 to yield 7.09 percent, compared with 7.17 percent on Monday, following the release of tame inflation data in the U.S. consumer price index report for March.
The Dow Industrials also advanced with a leap of 135.26 points, or 2.1 percent, to 6,587.16.
The Hang Seng surged from the open, stimulated by expectations of short covering demand for derivative issues and a feeling that recent declines were overdone.
Despite the rally, most brokers and analysts were cautious in their outlook.
"It's all helter skelter now," said Wong. "It is all interest rates and one has to be careful now. The U.S. market is looking overvalued and fragile."
Chartists agree Hong Kong looks weak despite the rally.
"I am not ultra bearish, but we look like we are facing a six to nine month bear market in the blue chips," said John Schofield, regional technical analyst at NAVA SC Securities.
The chief reason is the property cycle has turned, said Schofield, adding that he was basing his view on perceived drop in sales prices of yet-to-be completed flats in the secondary market.
Properties led the market followed by banks.
Henderson Land led the sector with a gain of HK$2.25 to HK$65.00, followed by Cheung Kong which also put on HK$2.25 to close at HK$66.75.
Index heavyweight HSBC Holdings, the most actively traded issue, jumped HK$4.00 to HK$186.50 on heavy trade of HK$870.92 million.
H shares rallied late in the day. Qingling Motors gained HK$0.225 to HK$4.475 and Tsingtao Brewery jumped HK$0.35 to HK$3.85.
